findings.title: An empty or legacy-free kinds declaration from one client turns interferences off for the whole ranked table
findings.reason: I confirmed this in the code. In packages/protocol/src/interferenceKinds.ts, parseDeclaredInterferenceKinds (line 27) keeps any array of up to 16 short strings, including [] and ['x']. The test at interferenceKinds.test.ts:63 expects [] to be kept. At line 44, roomInterferenceKinds replaces only an undefined declaration with LEGACY_INTERFERENCE_KINDS, so a declaration of [] makes the intersection []. Both server paths pass the client's raw value straight through. In matchmaking: room.ts:99, then service.ts:279 (enqueue), then service.ts:717 (matchRules). In private rooms: GameRoom.ts:516 (joinLobby), then GameRoom.ts:614 (gameRules). With an empty list, the engine refuses every kind with badKind (engine.ts:638), and view.ts:166 sets canInterfere=false, so view.interference is null for every player. One modified client can therefore switch interferences off for the whole ranked table, including between the honest players. That goes against D44 (INTERFERENCES_BY_MODE.ranked = true) and the CLAUDE.md rule that the server is authoritative. Honest apps never send such a list: onlineClient.ts:138 and matchmaking.ts:159 always send all of INTERFERENCE_KINDS. Every app since 1.0.0 supports the legacy three, so a declaration without them can only be a lie. One part of the claim is overstated: making yourself immune is weak, because a tampered client can already refuse to draw the effects, which only run on the victim's device. The real harm is that one client switches off a ranked mechanic for everyone, which it could not do without this path. Severity is low and nothing crashes. The suggested fix is cheap and correct: make the legacy three a minimum for every declaration, and update the protocol tests that expect [] (line 63) and [['cats'],['warp']] → [] (line 35).

findings.title: Interference refused for a general reason (paused, gameOver, disconnected, notActive) gives no 'not sent' toast after the launch cue and the 'launched' announcement
findings.reason:
I confirmed this in the code. It is low severity and mainly matters for 'paused'.

1. **Which refusals get the toast.** INTERFERENCE_REFUSALS (arsenalModel.ts:138-146) holds only interferencesOff, badKind, badTarget, targetOut, targetDisconnected, targetBusy and notEnoughPoints. GameScreen.tsx:842-850 shows the arsenal.refused toast only when isInterferenceRefusal(e.reason) is true.

2. **The refusal carries no action type.** effectsOf (effects.ts:68-76) turns any 'rejected' update into { kind: 'refused', reason }. GameScreen therefore cannot tell a refused interfere from a refused select or place. That is why 'paused' had to be left out.

3. **The missing reasons do happen.**
   - The engine refuses an interfere with notActive or disconnected (engine.ts:560-562), gameOver (engine.ts:500), and 'paused' first of all in the interfere case (engine.ts:634).
   - RemoteGameHost.act() refuses with 'disconnected' when the room is not live (remoteGameHost.ts:517-521). playOffline does not play interferences offline.

4. **The cue and announcement come first.** The launch is optimistic. useArsenal.launch plays cue('launch') and calls onLaunch (useArsenal.ts:119-128). ArsenalOverlay.onKind then announces 'arsenal.live.launched' and may draw the ripple (ArsenalOverlay.tsx:233-236), all before the host answers.

5. **A real race exists.** In a duel (freezeUpToPlayers=2), the opponent's hard drop, or the end of their soft phase, freezes the game on the server. A kind tapped before the paused view arrives (while blockedBy is still null) comes back refused with 'paused'. No toast follows. The player heard "launched" and gets no correction.
   - The pause overlay does show and no points are taken, so the harm is small.
   - The reviewer's 3–4 player example only applies once two players are left in the game.

6. **This departs from the lane's own design.** interference-ui.json says to map a 'refused' effect with reason targetBusy, notEnoughPoints, targetOut, targetDisconnected, interferencesOff, badKind **or paused** to the arsenal.refused toast. The code leaves 'paused' out, and arsenalModel.test.ts:228 asserts isInterferenceRefusal('paused') === false. DECISIONS.md does not rule otherwise.

7. **The fix is right.** The proposed fix (carry action.type in the 'refused' UiEffect and toast for any refused interfere) addresses the root cause, without making a refused select show the interference toast.

8. **Not a hard-rule break.** The gameOver and notActive cases matter little: the results screen follows, or the button is hidden. This breaks no CLAUDE.md rule; it is a UX and accessibility gap against the investigated design.

findings.title: iOS: keypad finger count double-counts multi-touch starts, so a phantom finger can cancel a keypad hit or keep the keys scrambled after it
findings.reason:
I could not refute it. The claim matches the code.

1. The finger count works as described. In apps/mobile/src/components/board/Keypad.tsx:61, `fingersIn` returns `changedTouches.length`. Lines 81-82 and 87-89 add or subtract that number on the row's raw onTouchStart, onTouchEnd and onTouchCancel. That number goes straight into `KeypadShuffler.touches` (apps/mobile/src/components/interference/keypadModel.ts:117), through the guard in useKeypadShuffle.ts:59. The shuffler keeps only a running number. It does not track touch identifiers or check against `nativeEvent.touches`.

2. iOS sends events the way the reviewer says. The project uses React Native 0.86.3, which only has the new architecture (Fabric). In node_modules/react-native/React/Fabric/RCTSurfaceTouchHandler.mm, `_dispatchActiveTouches` builds one TouchEvent whose changedTouches holds every touch from the same touchesBegan or touchesEnded set. It then calls `onTouchStart` or `onTouchEnd` once for each unique event emitter. TouchEventEmitter.cpp uses a plain `dispatchEvent` for touchStart, touchEnd and touchCancel, so these are not merged. Only touchMove is merged, through `dispatchUniqueEvent`. Each copy bubbles to its target's ancestors.

Scenario (a): two fingers land on two keys in the same frame. That is two emitters, so the row gets +2 twice (+4). If the fingers lift separately, it gets -1 and -1, so the count stays at 2. Scenario (b): one finger lands on a key and one on the board in the same frame. The row gets +2. The board finger's lift goes only to the board's emitter, which is not inside the row, so the count stays at 1.

3. The failure is real. `sync()` (keypadModel.ts:175) delays every shuffle while `fingersAt(now) > 0`. The extra count is only dropped after STUCK_FINGERS_MS = 10 000 ms with no keypad event, and every key tap moves `touchedAt` forward (+1 then -1, so the count never reaches 0). So:
- A 5 s 'keypad' hit that arrives within 10 s of the extra count never shuffles. The paid hit does nothing, which breaks D47 (the keys must swap every 1.5 s).
- If the extra count appears after the keys have moved, they stay out of order after endsAt for as long as the player keeps tapping keys. That breaks spec §7.1 ("outside these 5 s the keypad is always 1-9").

4. The tests don't catch it. Keypad.test.tsx:278-282 and useKeypadShuffle.test.tsx:128-131 only fire one event with one changed touch each time.

How likely: it needs two touches that begin, or end, in the same iOS touch frame (about 8-16 ms), so it happens occasionally, not every game. Even so, the code is wrong and the failure is real. The fix the reviewer proposes is sound: track touch identifiers in a Set, and drop any identifier that is missing from `nativeEvent.touches`.

findings.title: Keypad reduced-motion swap: withDelay skips its delay under the system Reduce Motion setting, so keys jump while still visible
findings.reason:
I checked the code and the claim holds. Keypad.tsx:179 calls `x.set(withDelay(half, withTiming(shift, timing(0))))` and passes no third argument.

How Reanimated 4.5.1 treats this:
- In delay.ts, an omitted argument leaves the delay's `reduceMotion` undefined (`getReduceMotionForAnimation(undefined)`).
- `decorateAnimation` (util.ts, the isHigherOrder branch) then fills it in at start with `getReduceMotionFromConfig()`, which returns the system setting (`isReduceMotionOnUI.value`).
- delay.ts:50 (`if (now - startTime >= delayMs || animation.reduceMotion)`) then starts the inner animation at once. The inner `withTiming` uses `timing(0)` (ReduceMotion.Never, 0 ms), so the key jumps to its new slot on the first frame.
- The opacity `withSequence` is not affected. Its children set `reduceMotion` explicitly, false via Never, and `findNextNonReducedMotionAnimationIndex` does not skip them. The fade-out and fade-in still play.

When it happens: `guard.reduce` comes from `useReduceMotion()` (GameScreen.tsx:308 into useKeypadShuffle). The setting's default is 'system' (state/settings.ts:41). With the default setting and the phone's Reduce Motion on, all the keys teleport to the new order while fully visible, then blink out and back. With the app setting 'on' and the system off, the delay works and the fade hides the move.

Why it matters:
- It breaks D47's reduced-motion ruling ("one permutation with a fade"), which is meant to hide the move.
- It also contradicts the file's own rule in components/board/animation.ts: "the system setting must not skip a variant that was already chosen".
- The project already passes the flag elsewhere for the same reason, e.g. connection/motion.ts:102 `withDelay(..., NEVER_REDUCE)`.
- Jest does not catch it because the system flag is off in tests.

Severity is low: the result is still static, so the CLAUDE.md Reduced Motion rule itself is not violated, and the input guard still voids presses during the swap. It is a real defect against the ruling.

Fix: `withDelay(half, withTiming(shift, timing(0)), ReduceMotion.Never)`.

findings.title: No test for D46 'only the victim sees it' (sender and third players keep a bright board and an unshuffled keypad)
findings.reason:
I checked the claim in the code and it holds. It is a low-severity gap in the tests, not a bug: the app behaves correctly today.

1. **No screen test covers the sender or a third player.** All three tests in GameScreenHit.test.tsx (lines 63-111) use hitBy(), where the bot hits me. None renders the screen of the player who sent the hit, or of a player who watches it.
2. **The sender test in GameScreenDuel does not check this.** "two taps…" (lines 402-425) checks only the view (players[1].hitBy, the score) and that the picker closes. It never looks for board-hit or hit-dim, and never reads the key-<d>-place positions.
3. **The third-player test in GameScreenGroup checks nothing on my screen.** In "a hit between two others" (line 335), the line commented "Not on me" calls queryByTestId('hit-banner') without `hidden`. The banner inside the game screen is rendered as 'hit-layer-banner' (HitLayer.tsx:177), so that query finds nothing whatever happens. It does not check board-hit, hit-dim or the keys either.
4. **The rule exists.** docs/01-SPEC.md:483 says "רק מי שנפגע רואה אותה. השולח והשחקנים האחרים לא", and docs/design/components.md:744 says the same.

Why it works today: GameScreen.tsx builds one `hit` from hitOf(view), which reads me.hitBy (hitModel.ts:54-56). That same value feeds HitLayer (line 1398), BoardHitLayer (line 1375) and useKeypadShuffle (line 957). One test already guards this indirectly: interferenceRanked.e2e.test.tsx:194, on the sender's side, checks that 'hit-layer-region' is absent. If hitOf ever returned the sender's hit, that test would fail.

But no test would catch the refactor the reviewer describes: if the board's dim, the scrambled digits or the moving keys were ever fed from somewhere other than the view's me.hitBy (for example, the interference event), they could appear on the sender's or a watcher's screen. Nothing fails today, and no rule from DECISIONS.md or CLAUDE.md is broken (CLAUDE.md requires a test for every engine rule; this is screen behaviour). So it is a valid, low-severity gap.

The fix the reviewer suggests is sound: in the sender and third-player tests, check that board-hit (with hidden) is absent and that every key's translateX is 0. The GameScreenGroup check should also query 'hit-layer-banner' with `hidden`.

fixes.summary:
Fixed all three confirmed defects in the mobile-effects lane.

(1) iOS phantom finger. The keypad no longer adds up `changedTouches.length`. A new pure function, `fingersOnKeys` in Keypad.tsx, keeps a Set of touch identifiers:
- On start, a finger joins only when it is in this copy's iOS `targetTouches`. Android sends no targetTouches and one finger per event, so there every changed touch counts.
- On end or cancel, the ended ids are removed.
- On every event, any id missing from `nativeEvent.touches` is dropped, so a lift the row never heard leaves no phantom.
- The row reports the absolute count. `KeypadGuard.touches(delta)` became `fingers(count)`, and `KeypadShuffler.touches(delta)` became `fingers(count)` (private field renamed to `down`). The 10 s STUCK_FINGERS_MS fallback stays. useKeypadShuffle passes `shuffler.fingers`.

(2) Reduced-motion swap. `withDelay` (and the fade `withSequence`) now get `ReduceMotion.Never`, so the phone's own Reduce Motion no longer skips the delay. Before, the keys jumped in sight. A new test turns on the system setting with `<ReducedMotionConfig mode={ReduceMotion.Always}>`. I checked that it fails without the fix and passes with it.

(3) D46 'only the victim sees it' had no test on the sender's or a watcher's screen:
- GameScreenHit has a new `it.each` for scramble, keypad and cats where I hit the bot. It checks there is no board-hit, hit-dim, hit-scramble or hit-layer-banner on my screen, and that all nine keys stay at translateX 0 after 1.6 s.
- GameScreenDuel 'two taps…' now checks there is no board-hit or banner on the sender's screen.
- In GameScreenGroup, 'a hit between two others' now queries the real 'hit-layer-banner' (with hidden) and board-hit. A new group test has Pip send keypad to Biscuit and Biscuit send scramble to Pip, and checks my board and keys stay untouched.

The iOS scenarios from the finding are now Keypad and useKeypadShuffle tests: two keys in one frame give 2 fingers, not 4, then 0 after both lifts, and a later keypad hit still shuffles; a key finger plus a board finger in the same frame count as 1.
